analysis:
This PR changes documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md (new paragraph at head lines 1030-1048, outside the supplied head text excerpt, visible only via patch) and docs/developer/test.md (new 'Prompt Preparation And Admission' section, head lines 322-345). No executable code, config or deployment changes are present in the supplied evidence, so I found no concrete security regression.

The docs describe a new PromptTokenCache in the provider (LocalTokenizerBridge, PromptTokenCache.swift), which reuses token IDs of prompt pieces within a prefix-cache scope. Security-relevant claims to verify in the code PR (not supplied here): (1) reuse never crosses a cache scope (relevant to T-041/SEC-035 and A-001 cross-tenant isolation). If the token-ID cache were keyed without the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, it could add a cross-account timing or content oracle. (2) The cache holds prompt-derived material in process memory (A-001, T-014), and it must not be persisted to disk; the docs do not say it is. (3) The cache is bounded in memory, which matters for availability under adversarial consumers. (4) The ChatTemplateLoopRewrites rewrites change template rendering, so a rendering divergence could alter the prompt actually served. The docs say load-time and sampled background comparisons disable reuse on a mismatch. (5) The opt-out DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 is documented; it is distinct from the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch. (6) The docs mention parallel encoding on up to four cores and a merged admission body decode (InboundChatRequestDecode) and cold-load serve-loop changes. These touch the coordinator-provider request admission boundary (TB-002) and should be reviewed in the source change.

The threat model (T-041 scope) may need a note that the in-process token-ID cache is scoped per prefix-cache scope, if the code change confirms it. The test doc adds a benchmark flag and PROMPT_TOKEN_CACHE_MODEL_DIRS, which are test-only. Because the implementation is not supplied, I flag needs_deeper_review for the code-side scoping and bounding guarantees.
